{{Navbar-GOGPT-tracker}}
'''Chonburi Ng Project power station''' is an operating power station of at least 2500-megawatts (MW) in Khao Khansong, Sriracha District, Chon Buri, Thailand.
It is also known as Gulf Sriracha, Gulf SRC, GSRC.

==Ownership Tree==

This ownership tree is part of the [https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-energy-ownership-tracker/ Global Energy Ownership Tracker], a project of Global Energy Monitor.

{{#widget:ObservableOwnershipTree|}}

==Background==

Mitsui & Co., Ltd. entered into a project finance agreement with Gulf Energy Development Public Company Limited for a gas-fired thermal power generation project in November 2018.<ref name="Mitsui">[https://www.mitsui.com/jp/en/release/2018/1227529_11215.html Mitsui to Move Forward with Gas-fired Thermal Power Plant Project in Chonburi Province, Thailand], Mitsui website, Nov 9. 2018</ref> They announced that Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems, Ltd. will be the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor.<ref>[https://www.mhps.com/news/20180209.html MHPS Receives Order to Construct 5,300MW Power Plant Project in Thailand Incorporating Eight M701JAC Gas Turbines], MHPS website, Feb 9, 2018</ref>

''Kaohoon.com'' reported that construction started on December 3, 2018.<ref>[https://www.kaohoon.com/content/268336 GULF เดินหน้าโรงไฟฟ้า”GSRC” 2,500MW รับลูกกกพ.ไฟเขียวพื้นที่สร้างสายส่ง พร้อมCODมี.ค.64], ''Kaohoon.com'', Dec 14, 2018</ref>

In December 2019, Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems shipped the first eight turbines to Bangkok, four for this plant and four for the [[Rayong Gulf PD power station]].<ref>[https://www.power-eng.com/2019/12/06/mhps-ships-jac-turbines-for-ccgt-plant-in-thailand/#gref MHPS ships JAC turbines for CCGT plant in Thailand], ''Power Engineering'', Dec. 6, 2019</ref>

The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand plans to commission two units in 2021 and the remaining two in 2022.<ref name="egatAnnual19">[https://www.egat.co.th/en/images/annual-report/2019/annual-report-2019-en.pdf Annual Report 2019], Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, accessed Feb. 9, 2021</ref>

Units 1 and 2 started commercial operations in 2021,<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/51051/51051-001-esmr-en_32.pdf|title=Thailand: Chonburi Natural Gas Power Project - Environmental and Social Monitoring Report|last=|first=|publisher=Asian Development Bank.|year=May 2021|isbn=|location=|pages=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.gulf.co.th/en/pdf/onereport-gulf-2021-en.pdf|title=Annual Report|last=|first=|publisher=Gulf Energy Development Public Company Limited|year=2021|isbn=|location=|pages=}}</ref> with units 3 and 4 then starting commercial operations in 2022.<ref name="autoref_4" /><ref name="autoref_5" />

The total project cost for the four units is estimated to be US$1.55 billion.<ref name="Mitsui" /><ref name="NS">[https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/gulf-sriracha-power-plant-chonburi/?cf-view Gulf Sriracha Power Plant, Chonburi], NS Energy, Nov. 21, 2018</ref> In November 2018, 12 international financial institutions provided the project promoters with loans totalling US$1.15 billion, including a US$227 million loan facility from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation<ref name="NS" /> and a US$228 million loan from the multilateral Asian Development Bank.<ref>[https://www.adb.org/projects/51051-001/main Thailand : Chonburi Natural Gas Power Project], Asian Development Bank Project Data Sheet, last updated Nov. 5, 2024</ref> Gulf Energy and Mitsui together invested US$395 million as equity.<ref>[https://www.ijglobal.com/data/transaction/48821/sriracha-gsrc-ccgt-power-plant-265gw-ipp Sriracha GSRC CCGT Power Plant (2.65GW) IPP], IJGlobal Transaction Data, last updated Oct. 31, 2024</ref>
